So the ball is at cols 44-46. To the left: wall at 43, then sky at 31-42, then wall at 30, then green block at 25-29.
Now, the key question: what's the goal? I've deleted 8 of 9 blocks. Let me delete the last one and see what happens.
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the whole game. Let me think about what's happening with the waves and the ball.
Actually, I notice the maze structure changed between the "9 blocks" state and now. Let me compare:

So the green blocks at cols 13-17 and 19-23 (rows 37-41) were deleted, and now that area is sky (S). The block at cols 25-29 remains.
So deleting the blocks turns them into sky (S). That makes sense — the blocks were "filling" the sky area, and deleting them reveals the sky.
So the green blocks are like "obstacles" placed in the sky area. Deleting them clears the sky.
Now, what's the goal? Let me think. The ball is at the right side (cols 44-46). The sky area is mostly clear now except for the one block at cols 25-29.
Hmm, let me reconsider. Maybe the goal is to clear all the green blocks (make the sky fully open), and then the ball can move to the exit. Or maybe clearing all blocks completes the level.
Let me just delete the last block at (39,27) and see what happens. That's the clear next step.
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider whether deleting the last block will complete the level or trigger a new wave. Last time, after deleting all 7 blocks, the level didn't complete — instead, moving the ball right triggered a new wave. So deleting all blocks probably won't complete the level.
But this time, the ball is already at the right side. So if I delete the last block, maybe the level completes (all blocks cleared + ball at right)? Or maybe a new wave spawns?
Let me just delete the last block and observe. That's the most informative action.
